claims.summary: For every prime p, on near-permutations (one doubled hole) and on one-empty-pigeon assignments of unary PHP^{n+1}_n, plain or functional, a linear decision tree over F_p of depth O(log n) finds a falsified clause, by counting pigeons in hole sets or holes of pigeon sets; so the known hard distributions of the bounded-depth closure method (Byramji-Impagliazzo Remark A.4 at p=2) are easy at every prime. claims.summary: Column dichotomy for unary PHP^{n+1}_n on any bipartite graph G, any prime p: for a hole set H_0 with |H_0| >= n/2, if the systems {occupancy(h) = 1 mod p for h in H'}, over uniform r_0-subsets H' of H_0, hold with average probability at most delta, then for every eta in (0,1) a linear decision tree over F_p of depth O(r_0 log(2/eta)(log n + log(2/eta))) finds a falsified hole clause with probability at least 1 - 4 delta/3 - eta; boards without a matching covering n/2 holes are easy outright. So the closure method's probability property, if it charges these safe column systems, contradicts its distributional search hardness for every distribution on every board. Exempting the occupancy forms as Byramji-Impagliazzo Lemma 5.7 exempts column sums is blocked by safety: beside the n-p+1 fixed occupancy forms of the modular-collision distribution, a safe system has at most p further independent forms.

claims.summary: For unary PHP over F_p, p odd, the rank-one system x_{1a}+x_{2a}+x_{3a} = 2 (with occupancy equations, a having at least p further neighbours) forces a collision in hole a without forcing any cell, so closures defined by forced cells (one-shot, or iterated with matching propagation) fail the Efremenko-Garlik-Itsykson Delayer step at rank at most two. Any local-consistency notion requiring a 0/1 solution, monotone under implication over 0/1 points, with the leaf property and the Delayer step below rank m, must reject every system on m cells whose 0/1 solutions all collide there; for p >= 5 one equation can spread such collisions over p-2 holes, so a closure seeing them needs at least p-2 rows and holes.

claims.summary: For plain unary PHP on a bipartite graph over F_p: call a subspace U of forms theta-dangerous when the vertex-cover number of its support (rows and holes) is below theta dim U; a greedy closure adding minimum covers strictly decreases |S| + theta dim<F[\S]>, so it has size at most theta rank (O(p r log r) with the theta that the onto lemma needs). Local consistency (an existential witness S within a budget with F[\S] theta-safe and a 0/1 solution injective on S, trapped pigeons included) has the leaf property and weakening under span containment, and rejects the forced-collision examples. Its Delayer step through the greedy continuation is refuted: hole covers trap pigeons (x_{as1}+x_{cs1}=1, x_{bs2}+x_{ds2}=1, f = x_{kh}+x_{k'h}); expansion and a cover-choice rule are needed. No least closing set exists (x_{1a}+...+x_{ma}); for functional PHP one row-count equation needs a closure of |R| rows.

claims.summary: For plain unary PHP over F_p with occupancy equations col_h = 1 imposed on local consistency: measure danger of a subspace modulo the occupancy span W by the least cover number of a representative (theta-dangerous when below theta times the quotient dimension). The greedy closure strictly decreases |S| + theta dim(<F[\S]>+W_S)/W_S, so |S| <= theta times the rank modulo W; occupancy forms (block column sums included) are exempted without the safety cap of pigeon-row safety; with absorbed cells (a cell whose column is otherwise pinned) trapping pigeons, the empty system is locally consistent and the negations of hole and pigeon clauses are not; the forced-collision examples are rejected (the calibration family for theta > p-2); and if the system is safe modulo W with theta >= 2l and every hole keeps at least 2l free cells, the occupancy equations join the onto lemma. The Delayer step and the treatment of row sums remain open.

claims.summary: Two closures for plain unary PHP over F_p fail the Delayer step on the full board. Private holes: with k = ceil(theta) and 2k+p <= n, Phi = {x_{i h_i} = 1 (i <= k), sum_i x_{j_i h_i} = 1} has a collision in every 0/1 solution, yet the vertex-cover closure (with or without the occupancy quotient) accepts it with witness the rows 1..k, since a closure pigeon's hole may hold other pigeons; by the rejection argument some query on a locally consistent system of rank at most 2k has no locally consistent answer, for every budget >= k and every theta > 1 in range. Row sums: a closure by matching edges (each closure pigeon in exactly one hole) accepts {sum_{i in R} row_i = v} with |R| = ceil(theta), v != |R| mod p, n >= max(2|R|, p), but no answer to row_{i_1} is locally consistent (rank two).
claims.assessment: Counterexamples with complete elementary proofs, checked by a fresh-context reviewer. They refute the Delayer step of prop:unary-vertex-cover-closure and prop:unary-closure-modulo-occupancy, and of a matching-edge variant; they motivate the star closure of prop:unary-star-closure-delayer-step.

claims.summary: Over F_p, let Psi be affine equations in the cells of a bipartite graph between pigeons and holes in which every hole has a neighbour, W the span of the column forms and O' = {col_h = 1}. If Psi together with O' is consistent over F_p and <Psi> is theta-safe modulo W (least cover number of a representative at least theta times the quotient dimension), with theta >= l_q for the quotient rank q (the Alon-Linial-Meshulam number: (1-1/p)^(l-p+2) q < 1), then for every map d choosing a neighbour d(h) of each hole there is a 0/1 solution of Psi and O' with exactly one pigeon in every hole, equal to d(h) for all but at most l_q q holes. Proof: Edmonds' matroid intersection of the l_q-fold union of the switch-vector matroid with the column partition matroid, safety bounding the number of non-constant columns, then ALM Proposition 3.1.
claims.assessment: Working proof from imported theorems (Edmonds' intersection theorem, the Nash-Williams union rank formula, Alon-Linial-Meshulam Proposition 3.1), checked by a fresh-context reviewer; the extension from the complete board to bipartite graphs is the reviewer's remark, checked by the author.

claims.summary: Star closure for plain unary PHP on the full board over F_p (danger modulo the occupancy span, occupancy equations imposed): a witness is a set of closure pigeons, closure holes and an owner map, not necessarily onto; its pattern puts each closure pigeon exactly in its owned holes and each closure hole's only pigeon is its owner. With theta > 1: negated hole clauses are not locally consistent; negated pigeon clauses are (a closure pigeon may own nothing), but no system of rank below n/(p-1) with a 0/1 solution implies one (Olson). With theta >= l_r and rank at most r: locally consistent systems have a 0/1 solution with one pigeon per hole, and the Delayer step holds in one-node form: extending the closure greedily by the stars of a solution from lem:Fp-safe-forms-one-pigeon-per-hole gives alpha and sigma* with |sigma*| + 3 theta D* <= |sigma| + 3 theta (D+1) + l_r D. Along a single path the Delayer can keep one near-matching and the closure is at most 2 theta T after T queries, so the content is the one-node form.
claims.assessment: Working proofs, checked by a fresh-context reviewer, whose correction (the path form is easy, with a linear budget) is recorded. Not a closure theory for the random walk: no canonical closure, no pigeon-clause leaf, possibly quadratic budget along paths that re-choose the solution, and no hard distribution.

claims.summary: For the modular-collision near-bijection mu_E on unary PHP over F_p (p >= 3: n+1 pigeons onto the holes outside a fixed set E of p-1 holes, one hole h* receiving p+1 pigeons): queries constant on the support are exactly those additive on pigeons x (holes outside E); (1) if the cells are partitioned among k players, integer sums of hole labels give an O(k log n)-bit protocol finding two colliding pigeons, so communication bounds through simulations where players hold cells give at most d = O(log n / log p) for linear trees (lifted simulations are not covered); (2) K = O(log n) fixed rank-one queries separate every support point from each of its single swaps (p >= 3), so single-swap sensitivity arguments give at most O(log n). No linear tree faster than sampling (about (n/p) log_p(n/p) queries) was found.
claims.assessment: Working proofs of the two obstructions (elementary), checked by a fresh-context reviewer; the absence of a fast tree is evidence, not a theorem. Search hardness of mu_E was later proved up to depth about n^{1/3} (thm:modular-collision-linear-search-hardness).

claims.summary: Two simulation lemmas for unary queries over F_p. L1 (easy direction of the standard four-point test): if a matrix C is at distance dist(C) from additive matrices a_i + b_h, a random swap of two pigeons' holes changes Q_C = sum_i C(i, g(i)) with probability at least dist(C), for independent or bijective choices and, under mu_E, at least (1 - O(p^2/m^2)) dist(C). L2: for independent uniform bits and nonzero differences delta_k in F_p, |Pr[sum delta_k beta_k = v] - 1/p| <= ((p-1)/p) cos(pi/p)^t <= exp(-pi^2 t / (2 p^2)); if every delta_k = +-1 (rectangle queries) the maximal deviation is at least (sqrt 2 / p) cos(pi/p)^t, so about p^2 log(1/eta) swaps are needed; one swap gives only two values, so Byramji-Impagliazzo's one-bit localization does not transfer to odd p.
claims.assessment: Working proofs (elementary counting and Fourier analysis), checked by a fresh-context reviewer, whose mu_E version of L1 and lower bound in L2 were checked by the author. L1 is standard.

claims.summary: The marginal-bounds lemma: let G be a bipartite graph between pigeons A and holes B, |A| = |B| + p, in which every pigeon misses at most mu holes and every hole misses at most mu' pigeons, and nu_G the uniform law on maps g into G with one hole h* receiving p+1 pigeons (the set S*) and every other hole one. With b = |B| and F_1 = b - mu - mu' - 1: nu_G(g(i)=h, h regular) <= 1/F_1; nu_G(i in S*) <= (p+1)/F_1; nu_G(i, i' both in S*) <= p(p+1)/F_1^2; nu_G(h* = h) <= p! b^p / ((b-1) F_2^p) with F_2 = F_1 - p; and nu_G(g(i)=h, h regular) >= F_3 (1 - theta)/((b-1)(b-2)) for every edge, with F_3 = F_1 - 2 and theta = (2p+3)/F_1 + p! b^p/((b-1)F_2^p), hence pair marginals of order 1/b^2.

claims.summary: The graph swap-test lemma: if every pigeon misses fewer than |B|/3 holes of a bipartite graph G, every function C on the edges at distance dist from the additive functions a_i + b_h has alternating sum nonzero on at least a fraction dist/K of the 4-cycles of G, with K = (b(a-1)/((a-mu')(b-mu)))(1 + 3b/(b-3mu))(b/(b-2mu))^2 (K <= 7.3 when mu <= b/15, mu' <= a/15); in particular 4-cycle-invariant functions are additive. Example H: on the blow-up of the 6-cycle (each vertex adjacent to two of three classes) the function 1 on A_1 x B_2 is invisible to every 4-cycle, not additive, and its query is not constant on the support of nu_G (finite check: all values mod 3). Under nu_G with missing bounds <= b/15, a uniform pair of pigeons gives a detecting swap with probability at least dist/15.
claims.assessment: Working proof (plurality decoding with a cocycle check on triple neighbourhoods), checked by a fresh-context reviewer; the exact version and Example H confirmed by a finite check (72 random dense graphs, 3 blow-ups).

claims.summary: The modular-collision theorem: for every odd prime p there are C_p, n_p such that for n >= n_p every linear decision tree over F_p (arbitrary affine queries in the variables x_{ih} of unary PHP with n+1 pigeons and n holes) of depth d that outputs two pigeons outputs two pigeons of one hole under the modular-collision near-bijection mu_E (n+1 pigeons onto the holes outside a fixed set E of p-1 holes, one hole receiving p+1) with probability at most C_p d sqrt((d + ln n)/n); so depth Omega_p(n^{1/3}) is needed for success probability 1/2. Proof: swap simulation in dense graphs; combinations of queries close to additive are made additive by revealing the pigeons on their exceptional cells, the others are localized on fresh random pairs whose orientations are hidden uniform bits (Fourier bound for systems), with a transfer from the prior along fixed paths to the adaptive tree.
claims.assessment: Working proof, checked by a fresh-context reviewer. Search hardness only: the random walk of Byramji and Impagliazzo also needs a probability bound and a restriction. Novelty not checked.

claims.summary: The detecting-swaps lemma: for a dense class (fixed pigeons sent to distinct holes of H', and a remaining graph G' between A' and B' = H' minus those holes, |A'| = |B'| + p, such that G' and every G'-i-h satisfy the hypotheses of lem:near-bijection-dense-marginals with F_3 > 0 and theta < 1, every pigeon missing fewer than |B'|/3 holes; the class is all maps extending the fixed pigeons with the rest in the support of nu_{G'}): if L = a holds on the class, the coefficient matrix of L is additive on G'; if L != a holds on the class, no map has p-1 pairwise disjoint swaps changing L, and in the regime of the modular-collision theorem L is within 4(p-2)K_0/|A'| of additive on G' (K_0 <= 15). Hence, in that regime, a class implying an equation or inequation at distance eps from additive on the full board fixes at least eps m/4 pigeons or deletes about eps n m/2 cells.

claims.summary: The bounded-degree head-count lemma: let delta >= 2 and k <= s/4 and let H be q distinct subsets of [s] of sizes 1..delta (heads); with E the delta-sets containing a head and theta = |E|/C(s,delta) (theta >= q/(2^delta C(s,delta)), equality without 2^delta for delta-uniform heads), the number of subsets of [s] of size at most k containing no head is at most sum_{j<delta} C(s,j) + 2.3 C(s,k) exp(k(delta-1)/s - k theta/delta). Proof by Lovasz's form of Kruskal-Katona. For the kernel method's dense step at p >= 5 (delta = p-1, s = 15(N+1), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda))) it gives a threshold Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)) of distinct heads, against Theta_p(N^(p-1)) possible; at delta = 2 it sharpens (DH-count).

claims.summary: The all-prime graph criterion: for every odd prime p (delta = p-1), a polynomial inventory and sufficiently large N, on the separated sixteen-neighbor graph with s = 15(N+1) projected coordinates, a source of M complete accuracy-one blocks with old inputs of degree at most delta (all companions and coefficient fields) has no ordinary PC refutation through D >= 2p-1 when every block's nonlinear rank r_a in P_{<=delta}/I_delta(Gamma_H) modulo affine is at most R or at least Q_*^(p) = ceil(2^delta delta C(s,delta)((delta-1)/s + 5k/N + (Lambda+1)/k)), with Lambda = log(64(M+1)), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda)), T = (p-1)(H_* + delta R) + p and TD + k <= N/10^6 (so RD <= c_p N: R <= N^sigma polylog N for polylog D, R <= c_p N for bounded D). Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)); at p = 3 it is the ternary criterion up to constants.

claims.summary: The all-prime clique-head theorem: under the hypotheses of thm:allprime-low-or-dense-graph-rank-exclusion, blocks satisfying (CH_delta-hyp) for some coordinate set M of size m_*^(p) = ceil((2s/k)(5k^2/N + Lambda + log(C_delta/2))) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) also join the criterion, where (CH_delta-hyp) asks that every delta-subset of M be a leading monomial of span(inputs) + projected old ideal under the degree-then-M-weight-then-lex order. Lemma CH_delta: a head family containing all delta-subsets of an m-set leaves at most 2 C_delta binom(s,k) exp(-mk/(2s)) sets of size at most k free, with C_delta = (4(delta-1))^(delta-1) e^(1/4-(delta-1)). Random dense blocks with h >= (binom(m,delta) ln p + Lambda)/ln(1/eps_p) inputs satisfy it, eps_p = 1-(1-1/p)^delta, so the threshold for them is Theta_p((N log N)^((p-1)/2)) instead of N^(p-3/2).
claims.assessment: Working proof, transcribing the ternary clique-head refinement; checked by a fresh-context reviewer. The random-block count uses a multilinear Schwartz-Zippel bound and a plain union bound, weaker in constants than the ternary stratified count. The old relations alone cannot satisfy the hypothesis, so a block whose input span has dimension below (2s/k) log(8(M+1)) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) never does; whether large structured common-factor blocks such as the sunflower family satisfy it is not decided, since their inputs give no coefficient on the relevant delta-subsets but cancellation against the old relations is not excluded. The window stays open at every prime.

claims.summary: Top-size lemma: a normalized mixture of pulled-back restriction designs annihilating U, where all components at sizes outside a set I annihilate U and I meets the nonzero-weight sizes only at the largest one, has a normalized sub-mixture on I annihilating U. Applied, under typicality hypothesis (T), to the ternary endpoint designs and an inventory with n random tuples at every input count: every successful PC mixture contains a degree-D PC design for the old base plus the n tuples of one input count, built from components not required to handle them.
claims.assessment: The lemma is elementary linear algebra with a complete proof; the application is conditional on (T), dense-side rank preservation at every restriction the mixture uses, which has no union bound for families chosen after the inventory. A reduction of the sheaf-entry mixture lead to a one-count design problem, not a refutation of mixtures; the one-count problem is a special case of the window problem and may be easier.

claims.summary: Wide-conditioning conjecture: for each odd p and D there are t,Q such that ordinary unary PHP plus an affine system with linear parts independent modulo rows, every nonzero combination Q-robust on at least t rows, has no degree-D PC refutation. With the transversal special case of the constant-row clamp, a transversal meeting it excludes a compiled source; but any width-t span has dimension at most (N+2-t)(N-1) < N^2, so for about that many random blocks or more no transversal meets the hypothesis. Control: C_j=1 for j<N has width N+1 but a degree-two refutation, so robustness is needed.
claims.assessment: Conjecture, untested beyond its recorded one-form and two-form special cases at their own parameters; the r-parameter lift it needs is unproved and the projective proof does not port. The dimension bound and union bound are proved, and the control is a checked hand refutation. The ceiling limits the conjectured sufficient condition, not transversal or other constant-substitution designs.

formalization.scope: Informal conjecture, counting bound and hand control; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: States the natural many-form extension of the p-complex lifts; if true it would give quadratic reach for common affine conditioning, beyond the recorded linear endpoints, while its width hypothesis cannot reach polynomially many random window blocks.
significance.next_action: Test the conjecture at constant degree on small robust systems of rank above the one- and two-form cases, or prove an r-parameter lift; it does not by itself address the window.

claims.summary: Bounded-span equivalence: for affine forms y_1..y_d over F_p in Boolean variables and constraints c_j(y) of degree <= e with common zero set P in F_p^d, the base plus the constraints derives every f(y) vanishing on P (degree <= (p-1)d in y) at PC degree <= (p-1)d+e, since F_p[y]/(y_i^p-y_i) is the full function algebra; so constraints confined to a bounded span are equivalent to conditioning on their allowed patterns (P empty: refutation; P a point: affine relations); an elementary fact about functions of finitely many affine forms.
claims.assessment: Working proof (function algebra is a product of fields, degree-compatible reduction, Frobenius relations from Booleanity); the three-selector control is the case d=2.

formalization.scope: Informal; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Resolves constraints confined to a bounded span into pattern conditioning; with total density below one only positive-density restrictions and at most one point-pin remain.

claims.summary: Column-tensor exactness: over F_3, in the collision algebra without row relations T = tensor over holes of (F_3 + V_j), V_j^2=0, a linear form l with nonzero column parts in c columns has Ann_{T_k}(l) = l^2 T_{k-2} and Ann_{T_k}(l^2) = l T_{k-1} for all k < floor(c/2), and the second fails at k = floor(c/2). claims.summary: Counterexample to a truncated Dade lemma over F_3: the rank-one column tensor X = F_3[t_1..t_14]/(t_c^2) with six random linear forms z_i = sum_c lam_c(e_i) t_c (lam stored in rank1_large.json) is free over every single nonzero element z of the span over F_3bar through degree 3 (at most 9 of the 14 lam_c in any hyperplane, so c(z) >= 5) and has predicted Hilbert function W = (1,8,22,14) positive through degree 3, yet dim X/gX = (1,8,22,15): freeness fails in degree 3. So, for general column tensors, single-element freeness plus positivity does not imply freeness; a genericity (special-position) hypothesis is needed. The quotient is F_3[s_1..s_8]/(14 squares of linear forms); the version for the board's own tensors remains open.
claims.assessment: Refutation by exact computation, confirmed by an independent plain-NumPy recomputation; checked by a fresh-context reviewer.

formalization.scope: Exact modular computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Shows the batched mechanism for the joint selector count needs a genericity hypothesis beyond single-element exactness and counting.
significance.next_action: Measure how special-position defects depend on span dimension and whether each has a bounded-span core.
